title: Python for Infra Tasks: When & How

scenes.say: Ever wondered when bash just isn't enough? Let's see where Python makes infra tasks easier.

scenes.label: Python
scenes.sub: Teams expect Python for automation and API work.
scenes.say: Most teams now expect you to know basic Python for automation and calling APIs.
Here's the rule of thumb: use bash for simple command glue, Python for logic or APIs, and Ansible for managing lots of servers.

scenes.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, time, requests
URLS = ["https://app.example.com/health", "https://api.example.com/health"]
failed = 0
for url in URLS:
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
        ms = (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000
        status = "OK" if r.status_code == 200 else "BAD"
        print(f"{status} {url} {r.status_code} {ms:.0f}ms")
        failed += status != "OK"
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print(f"FAIL {url} {e}")
        failed += 1
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)
scenes.say: Here's a real example: Python checks health endpoints, handles errors, and times each request. Bash would get messy fast.

scenes.question: When should you switch from bash to Python?
scenes.wrong: Only when bash can't run commands.
scenes.right: When you need logic, handle APIs, or scripts grow beyond fifty lines.
scenes.say: Don't wait until bash breaks. Switch to Python when you need logic, APIs, or your script is getting long.
